callvale.chapter_entry: STARTUP.md B2, chapter 33 (stage 2, month 14): 30 customers ask for an API; one test program sends 200 requests per second. Each customer needs its own key and its own request limit; requests use the customer's Callvale sign-in; traffic is unpredictable; no instances for the API.
callvale.decision: new paths on the load balancer / API Gateway in front of the web tier / chosen: API Gateway with Lambda, 20 requests per second for each customer. Accepts: audio never passes through the API; functions stay small.
callvale.adds: REST API with usage plans and API keys; Lambda integrations; Cognito user pool authorizer. Stage 4: a WebSocket API.
callvale.facts_needed: per-client throttling through usage plans and API keys (d023, d024, d025); API keys are not authentication, so sign-in goes through a Cognito user pool authorizer (d026, d031); payload and timeout limits explain why audio stays out of the API (d003, d004, d005); REST API needed rather than HTTP API because usage plans exist only on REST (d020); Lambda integration and no servers to run (d036, d046); WebSocket API at stage 4 (d041, d042). The story never teaches a fact: if the canon disagrees, keep the decision and change the stated reason.

demand.question: Throttling levels and order: account level per Region, per stage and per method (stage settings), and per client through a usage plan (per API key, per method). In which order are they applied, and can a stage or method limit be set above the account quota?
demand.note: Order is stated: usage plan per-client or per-method, then per-method stage, then account per Region, then AWS Regional. Stage and method limits cannot be higher than the AWS throttling limits; per-client limits cannot be higher than per-account limits.

demand.question: Are usage plan throttling limits and quotas hard limits (the guide says best effort)? What should you use instead to control costs or block abuse (AWS Budgets, AWS WAF)? Include the exact caveat sentence and its scope.
